Good to Know

Frequently Asked Questions

Everything we know to tell you about ordering, shipping and coloring — asked plainly, answered honestly.

Ordering & Shipping

Where do I actually buy the books?

We're launching on Amazon on 15 October. Leave your email and we'll send you the link the moment it's live — Amazon then handles printing, shipping, tracking and returns.

How is it shipped, and how long does it take?

Amazon prints and ships every copy, so delivery times follow Amazon's own estimates at checkout and vary by location and shipping speed. See our shipping & returns page for more.

Can I return a book?

Yes, through Amazon's standard return policy, since Amazon fulfills every order. Start a return from Your Orders on Amazon.

Do you ship internationally?

That depends on Amazon marketplace availability for each country. Our books currently list on Amazon.com for the US, with other marketplaces considered as the collection grows.

Can I buy directly from this website?

Not yet, and not planned for launch — books will be sold through Amazon only. Leave your email and we'll let you know as soon as that Amazon listing is live.

About the Books

Who are these coloring books for?

Adults and teens who like relaxed, detailed-but-approachable coloring. Little Animals, Lovely Days uses bolder, simpler lines that also suit confident younger colorists.

Are the illustrations original?

Yes. Every character and scene was created for Craven & Quill rather than copied or traced from another book.

What size are the books?

All three books are 8.5 × 8.5 inch square paperbacks with about 84 pages, 40 of them original designs with blank backs.

Can I buy all three together?

Each book is a separate Amazon listing, so add each one to your cart individually. All three share the same size and price, so they make a tidy set.

Do you have digital or PDF versions?

Not currently. Every title is a printed paperback, sold through Amazon.

Coloring Tips

Will marker or gel pen bleed through the pages?

Pages are single-sided with a blank sheet behind each design, which helps, but we can't promise zero bleed-through with heavy alcohol-based markers. Slip a spare sheet of paper behind the page you're coloring and test new pens on a corner first.

What's the best way to color the pages?

Whatever you already enjoy using. Pencils and fine markers work well straight away; if you use heavy alcohol-based markers, back the page with a spare sheet of paper first.
